summary: Hideto Ono is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University. His career includes a post as an assistant professor (助教授) at Aichi Gakuin University, attested in 1991.
Hidetoshi Yoshizawa works in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Taisho University as a researcher (研究員, attested 1998–2008) and later as chief research fellow (attested 2017).

Hidetsugu Yagi studied at Kitano High School and the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909), and taught Arthur Waley. He held posts at Tohoku University (~1919–1932), Osaka University (~1932–1946), Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1942–1944), and the University of Tokyo (~1944–1945).

Hideyo Ogawa is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics who taught Shindo Kusumoto. He held posts at Hiroshima University as assistant professor (~1989–1999), Professor of Indian Philosophy (~1999–2019), and professor (attested 2026).

Hideyuki Matsumori is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at Soka University (attested 2006). He held posts at Soka University as an assistant professor (助教, attested 2015) and professor (attested 2026).

Himanshu Prabha Ray works in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, having studied at Panjab University, Cambridge, and Jawaharlal Nehru University. She was Associate Professor at JNU (~1980–2012) and Chairperson of the National Monuments Authority (~2012–2015).

Hinrich Middeldorpf was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums and the University of Göttingen (~1806–1811), held a post at the University of Breslau (~1813–1861), and taught Albrecht Weber.

Hiram W. Woodward is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard and Yale. He held posts at Silpakorn University, University of Michigan (1972–1982), University of Vermont (~1982–1986), and Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

Hirananda Sastri was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at DAV College and Oriental College. He held posts at DAV College, Panjab University, the Archaeological Survey of India, several museums, Jammu and Kashmir, and the Archaeological Department, Baroda State.

Hirofumi Isoda works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1961–1966), where he served as lecturer (~1966–1974) and associate professor (~1974–2001), and is attested as professor emeritus at Shimane University (1974).

Hirofumi Toda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a professor at Tokushima University (~1968–2001) and was a special member at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of Lotus Sutra.

Hiroko Kawanami is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott, and taught Shi Jiancheng. She held an appointment as senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).

Hiroko Matsuoka is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who pursued doctoral studies at Hiroshima University (attested 2006). She has held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (attested 2016) and the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

Hiromasa Tosaki was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyushu and Harvard under mentors including Satkari Mookerjee and Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He was a professor at Kyushu University (~1978–1993) and Chikushi Jogakuen University (~1993–2002).

Hiromi Habata, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned a Ph.D. at the University of Freiburg. She held posts at the University of Munich, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Hiromi Yoshimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Shindo Kusumoto and held posts at Ryukoku University, including as a full-time lecturer (専任講師, attested 1987) and further affiliation attested in 2006.
Hiromichi Kato works in Buddhist studies. He studied under Ryogon Fukuhara, taught Collett Cox, and held a post as lecturer (講師) at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).

Hiromitsu Ikuma works in Buddhist studies, having earned a doctorate from Tohoku University in 2019. He has held researcher posts at the Shingon Buzan Comprehensive Research Institute and Taisho University (attested 2020).
Hiromu Kitanishi was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University (~1945–1948) and later served as a professor there (~1969–1991).

Hironobu Minami works in Buddhist studies. He held posts as a research assistant at the Chion'in Jodo Sect Research Institute (attested 2015) and as an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
